plan.title: Lab 2 npm auth and path-placeholder traps are inconsistent with later isolated labs

narratives.Description: Lab 2 npm auth and path-placeholder traps are inconsistent with later isolated labs
narratives.Overview:
## What happened

Lab 2’s first `npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` failed with `E401 Incorrect or missing password`. The npm debug log named both `https://cfa.jfrog.io` and `https://registry.npmjs.org`. The host also warned `Unknown user config "always-auth"`.

The lab’s recovery path worked: preserve attempt-01, create attempt-02, isolate an empty `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, retry. After that, init/doctor/toolchain/accept passed on `@deftai/directive@0.112.0`.

## Why this is hard for a human

1. Lab 2’s start script begins with `export DIRECTIVE_TRAINING_ROOT="/absolute/path/to/directive-training"`. If a learner exports the real path *before* pasting the block, the placeholder overwrites it and start fails with `could not resolve the curriculum clone`. The prose says the path is learner input, but the snippet still contains a fake path.
2. Lab 2’s fixture has no `.npmrc`. Labs 5, 7, 9, 10, and the capstone all write a public-registry `.npmrc` and often use `env -i` / stripped `NPM_CONFIG_*`. A learner who survives Lab 2 via tribal knowledge never sees that later labs already solved this.
3. Lab 2 is a ~1000-line paste of zsh/PowerShell functions. Later labs are `node <helper> create|guard|install|...`. The UX drop is large.

## Suggested repair

- Require the learner to replace the placeholder, or read `DIRECTIVE_TRAINING_ROOT` only if already set.
- Give Lab 2 the same public-registry `.npmrc` + env isolation as Lab 5, and keep the E401 drill as a *provided* failure (it already has one).
- Consider a Lab 2 helper so humans are not asked to paste a page of shell for a 25–35 minute lab.
